questions.question: Nadir Shah, ruler of Iran plundered the city of Delhi in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1739.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nadir Shah,** the ruler of Iran, invaded India in **1739 **and plundered the **city of Delhi.**
 
• This was a significant event in Indian history as it marked the** decline of the Mughal Empire **and the rise of **regional powers**.
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion was **brutal, **and he looted the city's riches, including the famous** Peacock Throne, **which was later taken to Iran.
 
• The invasion also resulted in the death of thousands of** civilians and soldiers,** and it took several years for **Delhi** to recover from the devastation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nadir Shah** was a powerful** ruler of Iran** and is considered one of the most **successful military commanders** of his time.
 
• He invaded India to plunder its riches and also to avenge the **defeat of his predecessor, Tahmasp II**, by the Mughals in the **Battle of Karnal.**
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion of India was one of the last major invasions by a** foreign power **and marked the beginning of the end of the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Peacock Throne, which Nadir Shah took from Delhi, was later seized by the **Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Durrani **and eventually ended up in the possession of the** British East India Company.**
 
• The invasion of **Delhi by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1761** was also a significant event in Indian history, as it led to the weakening of the Maratha Empire and paved the way for **British colonial rule.**

questions.question: In the 18th century, the British fought ______ wars with the Mysore rulers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The series of four wars fought between the British and the Kingdom of Mysore in South India during the 18th century was known as the Anglo-Mysore War.
 
 
• First Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1767-1769 AD.

 
 
• Governor: Lord Verelst was the governor during this period.
 
• In the first Anglo-Mysore, the British, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against Hyder Ali.
 
• Treaty of Madras: Hyder Ali wins against the British. A defence treaty was concluded in 1769.
 
 
 
• Second Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1780-1784 AD.
 
 
• Governor: Lord Warren Hastings was the governor during this period.
 
• In the second Anglo-Mysore, Hyder Ali, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against the British.
 
• Hyder Ali defeated Colonel Bailey.
 
• Hyder Ali died in 1782 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War and was succeeded by his son Tipu Sultan.
 
• Treaty of Mangalore: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with the signing of the Treaty of Mangalore by the Tipu Sultan in 1784.
 
 
 
• Third Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1790-1792 AD.
 
 
• Governor: Lord Cornwallis was the governor during this period.
 
• In the third Anglo-Mysore, the British, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against Tipu Sultan.
 
• Treaty of Srirangapatna: It was signed by the Tipu Sultan in 1792.
 
 
 
• Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought in 1799.
 
 
• Governor: **Lord Wellesley** was the governor during this period.
 
• Tipu **died in 1799** while defending the Mysore capital, Srirangapatna.
 
• The threat of the French to the British ended by the year 1799.

questions.question: What was the main reason for the defeat of Sirajuddaulah at the Battle of Plassey?

options.text: Britishers cut the food supplies of Sirajuddaulah forces compelling them to surrender.
Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle.
Sirajuddaulah's prime minister misinformed the locations of Britishers.
Britishers knew the secret way to enter Sirajuddaulah's palace.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Battle of Plassey:-

 
 
• When **Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj Ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal.**
 
• The Company was worried about his power and keen on a puppet ruler who would willingly give trade concessions and other privileges.
 
• So it tried, though without success, to help one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's rivals become the nawab.
 
• An infuriated Siraj Ud-Daulah asked the Company to stop meddling in the political affairs of his dominion, stop fortification, and pay the revenues.
 
• After negotiations failed, the **Nawab marched with 30,000 soldiers **to the English factory at Kassimbazar, captured the Company officials, locked the warehouse, disarmed all Englishmen, and blockaded English ships.
 
• Then he marched to Calcutta to establish control over the Company’s fort there.
 
• On hearing the news of the fall of Calcutta, Company officials in Madras sent forces under the command of Robert Clive, reinforced by naval fleets.
 
• In 1757, Robert Clive led the Company’s army against Siraj Ud-Daulah at Plassey.
 
• One of the main reasons for the defeat of the Nawab was that the forces led by Mir Jafar, one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's commanders, never fought the battle.
 
• Robert Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Siraj Ud-Daulah.
 
• The Battle of Plassey became famous because it was the first major victory the Company won in India. 
 
• After the defeat at Plassey, Siraj Ud-Daulah was assassinated and Mir Jafar made the nawab.
 
• The Company was still unwilling to take over the responsibility of the administration.
 
• Its prime objective was the expansion of trade. If this could be done without conquest, through the help of local rulers who were willing to grant privileges, then territories need not be taken over directly.
 
• When Mir Jafar protested, the Company deposed him and installed Mir Qasim in his place.
 
• When Mir Qasim complained, he in turn was defeated in a battle fought at Buxar (1764), driven out of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was reinstalled.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was overthrown by British and sent to exile in Burma, after the revolt of 1857?

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah II:-**

 
 
• He was the **Mughal ruler **who was overthrown by the **British** and sent to **exile in Burma** after the** revolt of 1857.**
 
• He was the last Mughal emperor who ruled India from **1837 to 1857.**
 
• Bahadur Shah II was a **poet and a calligrapher** and was not actively involved in politics.
 
• The British accused him of being a part of the **rebellion and exiled him to Rangoon,** Burma where he died in **1862.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He​** **was a Mughal emperor who ruled** India from 1628 to 1658 **and is known for building the Taj Mahal.
 
 
 
• **Alamgir II:-**
 
 
• He** **was a Mughal emperor who ruled India from **1754 to 1759.**
 
 
 
• **Bahadur Shah I:-**
 
 
• He** **was a Mughal emperor who ruled India from **1707 to 1712. **

questions.question: What happened in Bengal, India, in 1770 that resulted in the death of one-third of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Famine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bengal Famine of 1770 **was a catastrophic event that resulted in the death of approximately** one-third of the population of Bengal**, which was then a province of British India.
 
• The famine was caused by a combination of factors, including a severe drought that lasted for two years, a failure of the monsoon rains, and the policies of the British colonial government.
 
• The British had imposed high taxes on the local population, which led to widespread poverty and malnutrition. When the drought hit, food prices skyrocketed, and many people could not afford to buy food.
 
• As a result, thousands of people died of starvation, and many more were forced to sell their land and possessions in order to survive. The famine had a lasting impact on the region and its people, and it remains a tragic and controversial chapter in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Chemical explosion - There is no evidence of any chemical explosion occurring in Bengal in 1770. Therefore, this option is incorrect.
 
• Massacre - While there were incidents of violence and unrest during the famine, there was no organized massacre of the population. This option is also incorrect.
 
• Slavery - Slavery was abolished in British India in 1843, so it is unlikely that it was a factor in the Bengal Famine of 1770. This option is incorrect.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

I. Tipu Sultan is also known as the Tiger of Mysore.

II. Tipu Sultan ruled over Mysore from 1782 to 1799.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Both I and II**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Tipu Sultan was the ruler of the Mysore Kingdom and he is known as the Tiger of Mysore.
 
• He reigned from 1782 to 1799.
 
• Tipu Sultan expanded the iron-cased Mysorean rockets and commissioned the military manual Fathul Mujahidin.
 
• The French commander-in-chief, Napoleon Bonaparte, sought an alliance with Tipu Sultan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Hyder Ali fought the first Anglo-Mysore War in 1767-69 at the age of 17 and then Second Angle Mysore in 1780-84.
 
• Hyder Ali died during the Second Anglo-Mysore War and then Tipu Sultan led Mysore.
 
• He reformed the tax system and imposed tax directly on the peasant and collected through salaried agents in cash.
 
• Tipu Sultan deployed rockets against the advances of British forces and their allies during the Anglo-Mysore Wars, including the Siege of Seringapatam and the Battle of Pollilur.

questions.question: Tipu Sultan became the ruler of Mysore in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1782**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tipu Sultan**, also known as **the Tiger of Mysore**, was the **ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore **based in **South India**.
 
• He was a **pioneer of rocket artillery**.
 
• He was born on **1 December 1751 **in **Devanahalli **and **died on 4 May 1799 **in **Srirangapatna**.
 
• Remembered as the **first freedom fighter from India**, Tipu Sultan is known for his **bravery and skills**.
 
• He had **strongly resisted **the **conquest of the British East India Company **in **southern India **and **he was reluctant **to **welcome them **on his **soil**.
 
• **Tipu ruled the kingdom of Mysore**, which he inherited from **his father Haidar Al**.
 
• He become **ruler of Mysore in 1782**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **On the 4th of May 1799**, the **legendary Indian ruler Tipu Sultan **was **killed**, **fighting the East India Company **Army.
 
• His **personal possessions **and **rich library were looted**.
 
• His **four swords are on permanent display **in **two renowned Museums **in **London**.

questions.question: In which of the following years was Bahadur Shah II deposed by the British and exiled to Rangoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1857.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor.

 
 
• **He was deposed by the British and exiled to Burma (Rangoon) following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.**
 
 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 had made a futile attempt to declare him the Emperor of India.
 
• He was captured by the English and sent to Rangoon where he died in 1862.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Revolt of 1857 began after the introduction of Enfield rifles enhanced the growing disaffection of sepoys.
 
• On 29th March 1857, a young sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, Mangal Panday fired at the Sergeant Major in Barrackpore.
 
• Mangal Pandey and Ishwari Prasad were hanged and the whole regiment was disbanded. 
 
• This became the source of discontent among sepoys and the immediate cause of the revolt.
